newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea wants inter-Korean food talks in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea wants inter-Korean food talks in Beijing.

text.p: The North Korean Red Cross on Tuesday agreed to hold talks with its South Korean counterpart for more food aid but insisted such contacts be held in Beijing, a South Korean Red Cross spokesman said.
In response to a proposal by the southern Red Cross society to hold talks on the Korean peninsula on July 22, the northern side also counter-proposed that the meeting be held on July 23.

The southern side, which is due to complete shipments of 50,000 tonnes of food aid to the hunger-stricken North later this month, offered on Saturday that representatives of the two sides meet again to discuss details of additional assistance.
The 50,000 tonnes of food supplies were agreed in May following a round of talks in Beijing, the first between the two sides for almost five years.
The spokesman said South Korean civic groups had pledged donations for "tens of thousands of tonnes of additional food" to North Korea.
The Red Cross is the only legal channel for private aid from South Korea to the North.
The relief supplies via the Red Cross are on top of $16 million worth of donations made by the Seoul government in response to an aid appeal by the U.N. World Food Programme.
Following the latest urgent appeal by the WFP, Washington pledged $27 million in food aid, bringing to $52 million its contribution for the year.
The aid is intended to combat widespread malnutrition, particularly among children.
Floods that devastated much of the country's farmland and industrial bases in 1995 and 1996 exacerbated Pyongyang's already severe food shortages.
